findings.change: None for U3. Put it on the design's 'later, when it hurts' list: the rule could measure against the starting diff of the first round after the last checked round.
findings.claim: The new rule only covers a run whose first rounds were never checked. Suppose round 1 was checked, round 2's builder wrote a candidate and then failed before its check, and round 3's correction changes nothing. Round 3 is still measured against its own starting diff, which already contains round 2's candidate, so it stops as a gap without that candidate ever being checked. That is the same symptom as finding 492, one round later. The implementation does exactly what the brief asks, so this is a limit of the design, not a build defect.
findings.evidence: unit_build_outcome.go:43-46 (reviewed tree): round 1's starting diff is used only when earlierProofExecuted returns false for every earlier round; once any earlier round's proof executed, the round's own build-before is used. Brief decision 4 and Scope U3 ask for exactly this.

findings.change: None needed. Optionally, return errors other than a missing record instead of swallowing them.
findings.claim: earlierProofExecuted treats every launch-store read error as 'never executed'. If a record exists but cannot be read (for example it is corrupt), a no-op correction made after a checked round would run the check instead of stopping as a gap. That costs one extra check run; it never ships unchecked work.
findings.evidence: unit_build_outcome.go:122: `if launch, err := runner.Manager.Store.Read(id); err == nil && launch.Executed()`. A missing record and an unreadable one are handled the same way. Decision 1 only covers ids that have no record.
